newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Schneider boss worried by govt EMU stance.
newsitem.headline: French Schneider boss worried by govt EMU stance.

text.p: Didier Pineau-Valencienne, head of Schneider and vice-president of the CNPF employers' lobby, said on Tuesday he was worried by the change in the French government stance on a European single currency.
He also said the most important thing was a strong euro currency capable of competing with the dollar.

"Yesterday's latest position worries me enourmously. I am for the euro and I want it to be a strong currency. That's the most important thing," he said on the sidelines of an Schneider's annual general meeting.
"I thought we were set on a sure course to the euro. That's no longer exactly the case. The markets moreover have understood that the euro has lead in its wings," he said.

France's new Socialist-led government asked at a meeting of EU finance ministers on Monday for more time to reflect on the EU budget stability pact, a pact that would enforce deficit control discipline with the threat of fines after the launch of the euro, planned for January 1999.
